title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3), and those three invocations correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We reconcile a preregistration wording inconsistency (regression‑rate vs success‑rate) by reporting the executed estimand (paired success‑rate difference) and release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865).

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate operator intent into network configurations (intent→config). For operational NetOps, correctness (no functional regressions), limited blast radius, and auditability are primary concerns. A commonly proposed architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes a configuration, a deterministic verifier checks functional invariants, and an automated repair step attempts correction if violations are detected. Despite interest, there is little preregistered evidence isolating the verifier's impact under a within‑task paired design with full archival provenance.
Research question. Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? We preregistered a confirmatory paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) and executed the plan end‑to‑end with artifact archival.
sections.related_work: Prior work addresses intent→configuration translation, LLM‑based code/recipe repair, and verifier/guardrail architectures. Representative examples include Cornetto‑style synthetic benchmarks and LLM→IaC evaluations (PreConfig et al.), verifier‑augmented self‑correction systems (CRITIC), and NetOps translation frameworks (MeshAgent). These works motivate verifier use but rarely provide preregistered paired inference isolating verifier effect with full artifact release. Our contribution is a preregistered, within‑task paired evaluation focusing on operational functional correctness and repair activity with complete artifact provenance.
sections.methodology: Preregistration & estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified a paired confirmatory design. Primary estimand: paired success‑rate difference Δ = P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline). (The preregistration alternatively phrased the target as a regression‑rate reduction; we report the executed success‑rate difference, numerically equivalent with sign inversion.) Tasks and generators. deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced 200 intent→golden‑config tasks constrained to verifier‑supported constructs (task generator and manifest archived; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Topology scales and vendor‑mix were prespecified as stratification axes; inclusion rules exclude tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs. Execution & treatments. Adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed paired episodes using gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). For each task a single shared initial generation was performed; the guarded condition ran deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and allowed up to one automated repair call when the verifier reported violations (preregistered). Logging & archiving. All prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, parsed IRs, seeds, and hashes were archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7). Analysis plan. Primary test: exact (two‑sided) McNemar on complete pairs with 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for the paired difference. Missingness policy 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both episodes failed); prespecified sensitivity treats failed outputs as regressions.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400; completed = 376; failed = 24; complete_pairs included in primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12. Provider call audit indicates model_calls_used = 203 and repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). Primary contingency (complete pairs): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both failure). Aggregate estimates (complete‑pair analysis): baseline_successes = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_successes = 188/188 = 1.0; paired difference Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. 95% bootstrap percentile CI for Δ (10,000 reps, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149]. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute Δ ≥ 0.20) was not met.
Repair activity. The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation record that repair was invoked 3 times (stage_counts.repair = 3); these three repair invocations correspond to the three guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). The archive contains the per‑episode provider traces and raw scoring records that map each repair invocation to its episode and to the scoring outcome. The primary aggregate repair summary is provided in Table 1 and per‑call traces are archived (see Disclosure and data pointers below). 
Stratified outcomes and requested subgroup table. Reviewer‑requested stratified outcome tables by the preregistered topology‑scale (small/medium/large) and vendor‑mix strata are computable from the full execution/task_manifest.jsonl (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865) because that manifest contains per‑task metadata including the prespecified stratification fields. The supplied manuscript evidence bundle (artifact snapshot used to prepare this paper) does not include a finalized labeled stratified summary table; hence we do not reproduce a derived stratified table here. We therefore (a) report the complete‑pair aggregate primary result above and (b) direct readers and verifiers to the archived task_manifest and raw_results (paths & SHA‑256s provided below) to recompute stratified counts deterministically (the preregistered sampling and exclusion rules are recorded in the manifest). This disclosure preserves artifact fidelity and avoids deriving strata from an incomplete snapshot.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement in success rate (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes that required repair. However this is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and is not statistically significant. Two operationally important causes are visible in the archive: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness was high (≈98.4%), leaving limited room for absolute improvement; (2) verifier coverage and task selection — the deterministic verifier supports a constrained feature set and, for the sampled synthetic task family, most LLM proposals satisfied the verifier or matched the golden config, so repairs were rarely invoked. Power and detectability. The realized discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) imply low realized sensitivity for large absolute effects; the prespecified sample size assumed a larger discordant proportion. The preregistered power calculation (≈80% for a 20‑pp absolute change under assumptions stated in the preregistration) therefore did not translate into realized power because baseline error rates were much lower than assumed. Operational implications. Verifier‑guided pipelines add auditability and can fix some failures (here, 3 corrections), but measurable benefits depend on baseline LLM error, verifier feature coverage, and task difficulty. Low repair invocation counts constrain conclusions about iterative repair budgets, blast‑radius reduction, and cross‑vendor generality. Reproducibility. All artifacts to reproduce per‑task outcomes, repair traces, and stratified subgroup computations are archived and checksummed (pointers and SHA‑256s below).
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Archived artifacts show repair was invoked 3 times and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; however low baseline error limited measurable verifier impact. We publish the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary baseline difficulty, verifier scope, model ensembles, and repair budgets.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4%) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.
